classification.difficultyReason: After comparing rectangle and polygon areas, devise an unsupplied equal-area construction, such as bisecting vertical boundary steps to balance gained and lost regions, and verify its area.

inlines.text: Mary observes that when constructing a frequency polygon on a histogram with unequal interval widths, the area of the polygon does not match the area of the histogram.
This discrepancy arises because the frequency polygon connects the midpoints of the tops of the bars, which does not account for varying interval widths.
Consider the following frequency histogram and polygon.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, graph beneath the continuation of question 30
spec.description: Three adjacent outlined histogram bars and a blue midpoint polygon, with arrowed axes and the printed ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied comparison graph is permanently visible; area calculations and the modified polygon occur only in answers.

inlines.text: Find the area of the frequency histogram.

answer.worked:
Add the rectangle areas.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{histogram}}&=(2-1)\times4+(3-2)\times3+(5-3)\times2\\A_{\text{histogram}}&=11\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Find the area of the frequency polygon.
Add the two end triangles and the two trapeziums under the polygon.

answer.worked:
Split the region at the polygon vertices into two triangles and two trapeziums.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{polygon}}&=\frac{1\times4}{2}+\frac{1(4+3)}{2}+\frac{1.5(3+2)}{2}+\frac{1.5\times2}{2}\\A_{\text{polygon}}&=2+3.5+3.75+1.5\\A_{\text{polygon}}&=10.75\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Mary wants to draw a modified frequency polygon so that it has an area equal to that of the frequency histogram.
How should Mary draw her modified frequency polygon?
Use the modified polygon shown: join
It bisects the vertical boundary steps and has area 11 square units.

answer.worked:
Mark the midpoint of each vertical boundary step: $(1,2)$, $(2,3.5)$, $(3,2.5)$ and $(5,1)$. Keep the first peak at $(1.5,4)$. The descending line through the middle two marked points reaches height 2 at $(3.5,2)$. From there, draw through $(5,1)$ to the horizontal axis at $(6.5,0)$. The first segment begins at $(0.5,0)$ and passes through $(1,2)$.

These coordinates follow from the boundary midpoints. Check the area using the two triangles and the trapezium:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{modified}}&=\frac{1\times4}{2}+\frac{2(4+2)}{2}+\frac{3\times2}{2}\\A_{\text{modified}}&=2+6+3\\A_{\text{modified}}&=11\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: The same three histogram bars with a modified blue polygon and matching marks on the halves of vertical boundary steps. Different marker counts distinguish unequal lengths.

mathematics.coordinateDerivation: The second segment has slope -1 through (2,3.5) and (3,2.5), reaching y=2 at x=3.5. The final segment through (3.5,2) and (5,1) reaches y=0 at x=6.5.
